text: Setting choice: Forgotten Realms, a small invented realm in the Border Kingdoms (south of the Lake of Steam), 1491 DR. The Border Kingdoms are a patchwork of tiny realms that rise and fall, so a new kingdom fits canon.
Lines: none requested. The player is 18+ and mature themes are fine; handle them with craft, not gratuitously. The X-card (typing X) still skips anything immediately.
Veil / table preference: the player must not be shown DM-only information (plot goals, NPC intentions, secrets). See the dm-secrecy block.

Table setup: solo player with one PC; grimdark tone; RoboDM rolls all dice; strict RAW with rules_audit=always; house rules: no encumbrance, unlimited ammo after first purchase, no food/water rules; OOC: prefix means out-of-character talk.

PC concept: Chadickith, a 7 ft, 318 lb Dodrud: a homebrew woolly-mammoth variant of the Loxodon (GGR), purely cosmetic with no rules changes. Tortoiseshell coat of lion-tan and bistre-brown fur. Egotistical know-it-all who gets humbled often. Starts at level 3, standard array, all sourcebooks allowed.
Chadickith backstory: as a child his village was wiped out by a blood-raged roc; he was rescued and raised by a fire giant.
House rule: firearms (DMG optional) are for Artificers only.
Ruling: the optional feats rule is ON (feats may replace Ability Score Improvements). Great Weapon Fighting is only available to Chadickith via Fighting Initiate (TCE) at an ASI level (4+).
Ruling: a Loxodon trunk may hold or carry an object, including a stowed weapon, but can never wield, attack with, load or throw a weapon (GGR is silent; DM ruling).

Ruling: Chadickith starts with a hand crossbow instead of his class's handaxes and javelins, a one-time DM exception to starting equipment. His starting bolts count as his first purchase, so bolts are unlimited.
Chadickith took Primal Knowledge (TCE) at level 3 for Nature. He plans Fighting Initiate (Great Weapon Fighting) at level 4.

Backstory canon (player): Okton developed a ritual that uses his own (infected) blood to create hunters of 'our order'. Chadickith belongs to this order. Whether he has undergone the ritual is unconfirmed.

DM decisions (secret): keep the Heartcoal = Yaga-Shura's burned-out heart (Bhaalspawn) origin. Chadickith does NOT know Okton forged the Crown of Ash. Approved homebrew story mechanics (never shown as rules to the player): roc beacon (a death within 30 ft of the loose coal lets the roc fix its location, arriving in 1d4 days); Ashblood exposure DC 10 WIS save; trying to break the coal deals 2d6 fire. Session 1 opening: scene A 'The King Burns on Highharvestide' (backup: scene B 'The Night Cart'). Calendar: the king died 26 Eleint 1491 DR; session 1 opens on Highharvestide.

Chadickith is 76 years old (rolled 1d21+59). He was 8 when the roc destroyed Hadrun, so the attack happened in 1423 DR. His parents were Berov (father) and Radanya (mother), both killed in the attack. Okton has raised him for 68 years.
Okton's hunter order is named the Order of the Banked Fire; members are called 'the Banked'. Chadickith belongs to the order but has NOT undergone Okton's blood ritual (the Quenching).

Ruling: Okton's blood ritual is how a character gains the Blood Hunter class (Critical Role Blood Hunter on D&D Beyond, 2020). It is allowed as a class, but in-story only through the Quenching. Its rules are NOT in the local 5etools data and D&D Beyond is unreachable from this environment, so check details (multiclass prerequisites etc.) against the player's copy before applying.

Player-supplied Blood Hunter reference (OOC): https://www.scribd.com/document/820591774/Critical-Role-Blood-Hunter . Consult it, or ask the player to paste the relevant parts, when the Quenching or Blood Hunter levels come up.

Session 1: Chadickith now knows the ember is the Heartcoal from the Crown of Ash, that it feeds the 'gladness' infection of the roc and Okton, and that it was stolen from Ivoard's pillow. He does NOT know Okton set it into the crown, its Yaga-Shura origin, or the Glad Choir. Isine (Oselle's household servant) is stable at the Watch triage tent with Wilash guarding. The steward, Lorard's quartermaster and Kitwin saw Chadickith with her; the coal is in a cold-iron box in Okton's forge.

Session 1: a hooded Pyrewarden woman at the Blind Barrel left Chadickith a grey burial-notice note: the knife that cut Isine 'was kept in the Pyrehouse', 'not every warden is glad of it', meet at the Ashward almshouse at tomorrow's dusk bell, and tell no one in a red collar. DM: the writer is a sincere junior Warden unsettled by the Glad Choir (intended as an ally, possibly watched or a trap if the DM wants to complicate). Unresolved.

Session 1: Garford Whitlock, a hired watcher, tailed Chadickith from the Blind Barrel for Lorard's quartermaster. He saw the Pyrewarden leave the note and will report it unless stopped. He claims the Lady Oselle's steward has two men watching Okton's forge. Chadickith grappled him with his trunk.

Ruling: a Loxodon trunk can lift only 5 x STR pounds (75 lb for Chadickith), so it cannot hoist a grown man off the ground; it can grapple, push and pull him. Earlier narration of lifting Garford was corrected: his boots stay on the stones. A slam is an unarmed strike (trunk, +4, 3 bludgeoning); knocking out needs the target reduced to 0 HP with a melee attack (PHB).

Session 1: Jorson, a plain-coated wiry man with Oselle's silver key pin, offered on the Lady's behalf: a private audience at the Ember Keep at dawn bell, 200 gp, a safe-conduct and the Keep's infirmary for Isine, in exchange for seeing what the old woman carried. Chadickith's Insight read him as sincere about the offer but ignorant of what is at stake; he is armed (blade at the small of his back) despite showing empty hands. Answer wanted by dawn.

Session 1: Chadickith let Jorson (Oselle's household) take the unconscious Garford Whitlock, saying 'you can take him or the copper vat can take him.' Oselle's men (three at least, two more hidden in the lane) carried Garford away, claiming the Watch's drunk-tank. Jorson left a silver key on a barrel lid (Ember Keep gate token, answer wanted by dawn). Lorard's quartermaster Fenwin Thatcher will notice Garford never reported back.

Session 1: Chadickith asked Okton directly whether he made the Crown of Ash. Okton admitted it: he forged the cold-iron band for Ivoard Hask in 1453 DR and set the Heartcoal himself, recognised it, and that is when the gladness began in him. Chadickith now KNOWS Okton forged the crown and set the coal. He still does NOT know the coal's Yaga-Shura origin, Okton's desertion, the Glad Choir, or what the Quenching costs.

Session 1: Okton told Chadickith that fire, hammer and pyre cannot break the Heartcoal; it can be undone only in a fire giant's forge fed with a fire giant's own blood, which means Okton, and he fears it may cost him himself. Chadickith does NOT know that destroying the coal would also end the Banked's gift, kill the roc, and likely kill Kitwin.

Junie, a ragged Ashward girl of about nine, told Chadickith that at night covered carts go into the almshouse dead-house and the sisters are forbidden to look. Chadickith told her the story of the roc attack and Okton.

Session 1: Warden Kaselle Redfern (late 20s, cropped dark hair, scar along left jaw, smells only of lye/ash/lavender) met Chadickith at the Ashward almshouse. She named Brother Peret, a lay-brother of the Pyrehouse's inner circle ('the Choir'), as the knife-bearer who killed at Isine; says covered carts bring Ashward dead to the dead-house nightly (19 counted in three months, all with the same smile). She fears the Watch is sold and the High Pyrewarden would hang her. Offers to show Chadickith the dead-house cellar when the midnight cart arrives. Chadickith's Insight failed, so he cannot tell if she is sincere (she is).

Session 1, almshouse dead-house: Chadickith hid in the coffin racks and saw Brother Peret and two Choir brothers bring a smiling dead man (50s, Ashward pauper) at midnight. A narrow closed stab wound under the ribs showed the man was killed, not plague dead. The Choir smelled strongly of hot iron and copper and the cellar warmed. Peret hummed a hymn and told the dead man to 'go gladly'. Kaselle is hiding behind the shroud-stacks.
